title: Proper morphism with a finite fibre is finite near the base point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $S$ be locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $s\in S$ be a point such that the fibre $X_s=f^{-1}(s)$ is finite. Then there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that the restricted morphism $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is finite.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near], recorded as Mathlib theorem AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_morphismRestrict_of_finite_preimage_singleton, to f, s and the given finite fibre. Its conclusion is exactly the required open neighbourhood and finiteness of the restriction. The theorem works over any base; the locally Noetherian hypothesis remains in our unchanged statement but is not needed by this specialization.
